chapter: Building McShann's big band and blues records
title: Front-line changes and Bird's comings and goings
summary: Earl Jackson, Piggy, Scotty and Bird swapped places in the band; Bird hoboed to New York and Lester came from Ernie Fields.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Now, during that time, sometime there in the fall, we had had Earl Jackson, we had many changes in the front line, then, Bob McShann (PHONETIC) was the only one that stayed there. There was a couple of trumpet players. Finally we got Piggy, then we got Scotty, and we got Earl Jackson. Then -for some unknown reason, Earl signed on (inaudible) and left, and we got Bird. And Bird messed up or something, and Max Hammond let him go, got Earl back. Earl had some trouble, and we got Bird back. And then we went -- Jay and I went away to Chicago.

And while we were gone, we left the band under the control of William Scott, the tenor player. He had that real business manner about him, you know. And so when we got back, Bird was in New York. Bird had hoboed, in fact he had come from Chicago, and we didn't even see him.

He hoboed to New York. Well, he hoboed, hitchhiked. Anyway, we said hoboed because he hoboed to Chicago, and then however he got to New York, we don't know. And so then McShann got Earl Jackson back again.
And now this is in the middle of '39, Bird comes

back. No -- no, I'm ahead of myself. We got a guy called Lester, something, out of Ernie Fields' band, and Earl Jackson. And it was then that McShann began organizing, bringing in the big band. John Tumino (PHONE) had leased --
